notes.claim: In a bridge rectifier the current flows in the same direction through the load whatever the polarity of the input.
The full-wave average output is 0.637 of the peak, twice the half-wave value, assuming no diode losses.
A full-wave bridge has a ripple frequency twice the supply frequency, for example 100 Hz from a 50 Hz supply.

sources.title: Rectifier Circuits | Diodes and Rectifiers | Electronics Textbook
sources.quote: Note that regardless of the polarity of the input, the current flows in the same direction through the load.

sources.title: Full Wave Rectifier and Bridge Rectifier Theory
sources.quote: the average output voltage for the full-wave circuit will be: 2 x 0.318V max = 0.637V max of the peak voltage. Assuming no diode losses.

sources.title: Full Wave Rectifier and Bridge Rectifier Theory
sources.quote: The ripple frequency is now twice the supply frequency (e.g. 100Hz for a 50Hz supply or 120Hz for a 60Hz supply.)
